Subject: Staged prepay options + Net90 request for milestone invoices

Hi Kimberly,

Thanks again for the demo last week. Orchid is enthusiastic about Redwood for inference — performance looks great. Procurement and finance have one remaining sticking point on commercial structure before we proceed to legal: Orchid prefers a staged prepay (to preserve cashflow) and needs Net90 payment terms on milestone invoices for Year 2 and Year 3.

Key asks from our side:
- A 3-year committed arrangement (target ARR equivalent $600k/yr, $1.8M total) but we want to split payments across milestones rather than a full upfront prepay.
- We need a clear ramp schedule (what percentage due at signature vs. annual milestone).
- If you can offer term discounts tied to multi-year commitment, list the tiers and how they apply to invoices.
- We also need a usage true-up mechanism and a potential shortfall credit (if we underutilize relative to commitment).

Procurement is explicit: they will only accept Net90 on milestone invoices (they cannot do Net30 in their system for multi-year milestone invoices without finance approval). Can you outline options and any controls Redwood finance would require to grant a Net90 exception?

Attaching our rough procurement checklist for context. Looking forward to a proposal so we can move to legal.

Thanks,

Sarah Kline
Procurement Lead | Orchid Labs

Sarah — really appreciate the clear asks. Below are two commercial structures that would meet Orchid's cashflow preference while protecting Redwood from receivable risk. I copied David in for finance input on the Net90 exception. I also attached a term sheet and an updated SOW (Orchid_SOW_v3.pdf) and a summary spreadsheet for payment scenarios.

Option A — Staged prepay (preferred for both sides)
- Commitment: 3 years, $1.8M total (committed spend).
- Discount: 12% term discount applied to the committed amount (applies pro-rata to the committed units/pricing).
- Payment schedule: 35% due at signature (prepay deposit), 35% due at start of Year 2, 30% due at start of Year 3.
- Year 2 & Year 3 invoices: Redwood can agree to Net90 on those milestone invoices subject to Finance-approved safeguards (see below).
- Usage true-up: quarterly usage reports; if actuals < committed, Orchid receives a credit that can be applied to future invoices or carried forward for 12 months, up to 25% of the year 1 committed spend (to balance risk).

Option B — Hybrid prepay + annual invoicing
- Commitment: 3 years, $1.8M total.
- Discount: 8% term discount.
- Payment schedule: 50% due at signature, remaining paid annually in 2 equal installments (start Year2 & Year3) on Net30.
- No Net90 option for annual invoices in Option B (standard Net30).

Finance safeguards (what we would need to approve Net90 on milestones)
- Signed SOW and PO attached to each milestone invoice.
- A refundable deposit (the 35% prepay in Option A counts toward this) or an increased deposit equal to 40% of total committed spend if Orchid requires Net90 on Year 2/3 invoices without a PO/guarantee.
- For Net90 exceptions > $300k per invoice, Redwood Finance requires either an irrevocable bank guarantee or an additional 2% fee to offset AR risk.
- Standard credit review; approval valid for contract term with quarterly monitoring.

Other notes:
- We can cap price increases year-over-year for the duration of the commitment; Lauren can follow up on ramp and throughput guarantees separately.
- We will include a shortfall credit mechanism in the term sheet language and can negotiate carry-forward mechanics if Orchid prefers credits vs refunds.

If either option looks close, I can draft the final term sheet and circulate to legal. Happy to hop on a call if you want to walk through scenarios.

Best,

Kim / Sarah — quick finance perspective. We are open to Net90 on milestone invoices for strategic, multi-year deals, but we need to limit exposure and have operational controls. Practical approach:

- For Option A (35/35/30), Finance will approve Net90 on Year 2 and Year 3 milestone invoices provided Orchid: (a) signs a PO for each milestone or (b) increases the deposit to 40% of total committed spend OR (c) provides an irrecoverable instrument (bank guarantee or letter of credit).
- If Orchid chooses PO route, invoices up to $300k can be Net90 without additional fees. For invoices > $300k under Net90 we apply a 2% AR risk premium (one-time on that invoice).
- We will require a quarterly review of usage vs committed; if usage falls more than 30% under committed levels for two consecutive quarters, Redwood reserves the right to move to Net30 for remaining invoices or request additional collateral.

If Orchid is comfortable with any of the three safeguards, please indicate which route they prefer and we will mark finance conditional approval in the term sheet.

Thanks,
